name: CA-23
label: Likely R

key_factors: Challenger Hodge's minimal fundraising and cash
model.rationale: The district's 9-point Republican lean, Obernolte's incumbency, and his overwhelming money edge — $1.6 million on hand versus about $10,000 for Hodge — make an upset highly unlikely, and prediction markets agree at roughly 96% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to the partisan baseline.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or a dramatically favorable national environment could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Jay Obernolte seeks another term in a California district that leans about nine points Republican. He advanced to the general election and holds a commanding financial position, with roughly $1.6 million in cash on hand after raising about $1.5 million, plus modest outside support. Democratic challenger Tessa Lynn Hodge has raised under $80,000 and has only about $10,000 available, with essentially no outside help.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, the incumbency advantage, and the stark fundraising gap. Prediction markets price Obernolte's chances at roughly 96 percent. The seat is expected to remain Republican, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
